page: The Amazon Web Services c6gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by AWS Graviton ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors running on the Nitro hypervisor. It delivers 32 dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core, eliminating CPU contention typical of hyperthreaded architectures. System memory is configured at 64.0 GB, adhering to a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio designed for compute-bound tasks. Bundled directly with the instance is 1,900 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, offering low-latency scratch disk space alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Discrete GPU acceleration is not present on this server type.

Benchmark metrics demonstrate balanced multi-core execution alongside predictable resource contention characteristics. In multi-threaded evaluations, the 32 dedicated cores produce consistent throughput in Clang software compilation, ray tracing, and stress-ng multi-core testing. In-memory workloads benefit from strong small-block cached memory bandwidth, driving 40.61 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core and compression tests, show lower baseline performance compared to high-frequency x86 platforms. Cryptographic tasks utilize native hardware AES acceleration, though vector extensions such as AVX-512 are absent on this ARM architecture.

From an architectural perspective, the c6gd.8xlarge offers high core density and power efficiency typical of Graviton processors, maximizing multi-core execution per compute unit without hyperthreading penalties. The inclusion of 1,900 GB direct-attached NVMe storage removes the need for networked volume overhead in I/O-intensive temporary operations. This combination is suited for parallelized build environments, distributed data processing, log analysis, video encoding, in-memory key-value caching, and microservices architectures requiring high parallel core counts with local storage buffering.
description: The Amazon Web Services c6gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. Built on the AWS Nitro System, it features 32 dedicated physical cores from an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation, avoiding simultaneous multithreading overhead. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage includes 1,900 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage for high-throughput, low-latency temporary data access, supplemented by a 12 Gbps baseline network capacity. The instance does not include a GPU. Benchmarks show reliable multi-threaded compute and caching capabilities, with balanced performance across multi-core stress testing, software compilation, and in-memory operations like Redis SET processing. Single-thread processing remains modest compared to high-clock x86 architectures. This server is best suited for scale-out compute tasks, CI/CD build farms, ad servers, caching nodes, and workloads requiring fast local scratch storage.
